name: Filesystem
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Read/write files inside directories you allow on the command line.
credentials: None
maintenance: Monorepo release v1.0.0 on 2026-10-11 publishes @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem 1.0.0 (npm); last commit 2026-10-10 (path-scoped)
install: Run `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem <allowed-dir>` from your client's MCP config (see README).
verdict: Pick it when the agent must read/write project files; scope it to the directories you pass on the command line.

name: Git
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Reads and modifies a local Git repository (status, diff, commit, branch).
credentials: None
maintenance: Monorepo release v1.0.0 on 2026-10-11 publishes mcp-server-git 2026.10.10 (PyPI); last commit 2026-10-10 (path-scoped)
install: Run with `uvx mcp-server-git --repository <path>` (see README).
verdict: Pick it for local Git work (status, diff, commit, branch) without a hosted account; it can modify the repo.

name: Fetch
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Makes outbound HTTP requests to URLs the model chooses; README warns it can reach local/internal IPs.
credentials: None

install: Run with `uvx mcp-server-fetch` (see README).
verdict: Pick it to pull a web page into context; the README warns it can reach local/internal IPs, so restrict it.

name: Memory (knowledge graph)
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Writes a local JSON knowledge-graph file.
credentials: None
maintenance: Monorepo release v1.0.0 on 2026-10-11 publishes @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory 1.0.0 (npm); last commit 2026-10-10 (path-scoped)
install: Run `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` (see README).
verdict: Pick it for persistent notes across sessions; it stores a local JSON knowledge graph, no cloud account.

name: Sequential Thinking
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: No external access; structures step-by-step reasoning.
credentials: None
maintenance: Monorepo release v1.0.0 on 2026-10-11 publishes @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking 1.0.0 (npm); last commit 2026-10-10 (path-scoped)
install: Run `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking` (see README).
verdict: Pick it to make the agent plan step by step; no external access and no credentials.

name: Time
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: No external access; time and timezone conversion.
credentials: None
maintenance: Monorepo release v1.0.0 on 2026-10-11 publishes mcp-server-time 2026.10.10 (PyPI); last commit 2026-10-10 (path-scoped)
install: Run with `uvx mcp-server-time` (see README).
verdict: Pick it when tasks need correct current time or timezone conversion; no external access.

agentsSource: anthropics/skills README (Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude API)

install: Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`, then install example-skills.

agentsSource: anthropics/skills README (Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude API)

install: Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`, then install example-skills.

name: web-artifacts-builder
agentsSource: anthropics/skills README (Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude API)
permissions: Runs local build scripts (React/Tailwind bundling).

name: doc-coauthoring
agentsSource: anthropics/skills README (Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude API)
permissions: Instructions only; edits documents you provide.
credentials: None
install: Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`, then install example-skills.
verdict: Pick it to co-write specs or docs; instructions only, edits the documents you provide.

name: pdf
agentsSource: anthropics/skills README (Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude API)
permissions: Runs local Python scripts that read and write PDF files.
credentials: None
install: Claude Code: `/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills` (see repo README).
verdict: Pick it to read, fill or generate PDFs; runs local Python scripts on your files.

name: GitHub MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Acts on GitHub with the scopes of your token/OAuth app: repos, issues, PRs, Actions (toolsets configurable, read-only mode available).
credentials: GitHub OAuth (remote server) or a Personal Access Token (GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN).
install: Remote: add https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ in your client; local: Docker image ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server (see README).
verdict: Pick it for issues, PRs and Actions from the agent; limit toolsets or use read-only mode for review tasks.

name: Playwright MCP
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Controls a real browser: navigates, clicks, fills forms, can access any site the browser can.
credentials: None
install: Add `npx @playwright/mcp@latest` to your client MCP config (README has per-client steps).
verdict: Pick it to let the agent drive a real browser for E2E checks; it can reach any site the browser can.

name: Sentry MCP
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Reads issues, events and projects in your Sentry org; can update issues.
credentials: Sentry OAuth (remote) or a Sentry user auth token (stdio).
install: Remote server https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp, or stdio `npx @sentry/mcp-server` (see README).
verdict: Pick it to debug production errors from Sentry inside the agent; needs Sentry OAuth or a user token.

name: Stripe MCP / Agent Toolkit
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Creates and reads Stripe objects (customers, payments, products) with your key's permissions.
credentials: Stripe OAuth for the remote server (other key options: see docs.stripe.com/mcp).
install: Remote server `https://mcp.stripe.com` via OAuth; connection docs at docs.stripe.com/mcp (linked from README).
verdict: Pick it to inspect or create Stripe objects; use the remote server with OAuth and a restricted scope.

name: Supabase MCP
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Manages Supabase projects: SQL, migrations, branches, edge functions; read-only and project-scoped modes documented.
credentials: Supabase OAuth (remote) or a personal access token.
install: Remote https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp (see README for flags like read_only and project_ref).
verdict: Pick it for Supabase SQL and migrations; use the documented read-only and project-scoped modes.

name: Cloudflare MCP servers
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Remote servers act on your Cloudflare account (Workers, observability, DNS analytics, docs) per OAuth scopes.
credentials: Cloudflare OAuth (per server).
install: Add a remote URL like https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp or https://observability.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp (list in README).
verdict: Pick it for Workers, observability and Cloudflare docs; each remote server uses its own OAuth scopes.

name: Context7
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Sends library names/queries to Context7's hosted service and returns docs.
credentials: Optional Context7 API key (higher rate limits).
install: Remote https://mcp.context7.com/mcp or `npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp` (see README).
verdict: Pick it for up-to-date library docs in prompts; queries go to Context7's hosted service.

name: AWS MCP Servers
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Each server acts on AWS with your local credentials/profile; scope depends on the IAM role.
credentials: AWS credentials (profile / IAM) for servers that call AWS; docs server needs none.
install: Pick a server from the README table, e.g. `uvx awslabs.aws-documentation-mcp-server@latest`, or the remote AWS MCP Server (preview) via `mcp-proxy-for-aws`.
verdict: Pick the specific AWS server you need; the docs server needs no credentials, others use your IAM profile.

name: Terraform MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Queries Terraform Registry; with a token, works with HCP Terraform/TFE workspaces.
credentials: Optional TFE_TOKEN for HCP Terraform / Enterprise features.
install: Docker image hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server or released binary (see README).
verdict: Pick it for Terraform Registry lookups; add TFE_TOKEN only if you need HCP Terraform workspaces.

name: Grafana MCP
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Reads dashboards, datasources, Prometheus/Loki queries, incidents; some write tools.
credentials: GRAFANA_URL plus a service account token (GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN) or basic auth.
install: Binary, Docker image grafana/mcp-grafana or `uvx` (see README).
verdict: Pick it to query dashboards, Prometheus and Loki from the agent; needs a Grafana service account token.

name: Chrome DevTools MCP
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Controls and inspects a Chrome instance (performance traces, network, console); README warns it exposes browser content to the client.
credentials: None
install: Add `npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest` to your client (README lists per-client steps).
verdict: Pick it for performance traces, network and console debugging; it exposes browser content to the client.

name: MongoDB MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Runs queries/admin ops on a MongoDB database or Atlas; read-only mode documented.
credentials: MongoDB connection string, or Atlas API client ID/secret.
install: `npx -y mongodb-mcp-server` with env vars from README (supports --readOnly).
verdict: Pick it for MongoDB or Atlas queries; enable the documented read-only mode for exploration.

name: Neon MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Manages Neon projects, branches and runs SQL with your account's rights.
credentials: Neon OAuth (remote) or NEON_API_KEY.
install: `npx neon@latest init`, or add the remote server with `npx add-mcp https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp` (see README).
verdict: Pick it to manage Neon branches and run SQL; it acts with your account's rights.

name: Notion MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Reads and writes pages/databases the integration is shared with.
credentials: Notion integration token (NOTION_TOKEN) for local; OAuth for Notion's hosted MCP.
install: `npx -y @notionhq/notion-mcp-server` with NOTION_TOKEN (see README; hosted option documented there).
verdict: Pick it to read/write Notion specs; it only sees pages shared with the integration.

name: Docker MCP Gateway
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Runs other MCP servers in containers on your machine; permissions depend on the servers you enable.
credentials: Depends on each enabled server (secrets managed by Docker).
install: Docker Desktop MCP Toolkit or `docker mcp gateway run` (see README).
verdict: Pick it to run several MCP servers in containers; permissions depend on the servers you enable.

name: Microsoft MCP (Azure MCP Server)
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Acts on Azure resources with your signed-in identity/RBAC.
credentials: Azure identity (az login / Entra ID).
install: See the repo README for the Azure MCP Server package and VS Code extension.
verdict: Pick it for Azure resources from the agent; it acts with your signed-in identity and RBAC.

name: Firecrawl MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Sends URLs to Firecrawl's hosted API to scrape/crawl/search.
credentials: FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.
install: `npx -y firecrawl-mcp` with FIRECRAWL_API_KEY (see README).
verdict: Pick it for crawling and scraping at scale; URLs are sent to Firecrawl's hosted API with your key.

name: Elasticsearch MCP Server (deprecated)
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Queries Elasticsearch indices with your credentials.
credentials: ES_URL plus ES_API_KEY (or username/password).
maintenance: Release v0.4.6 on 2025-10-24; last commit 2026-06-23 ; DEPRECATED per README
install: README marks it deprecated (critical security fixes only) and points to Elastic Agent Builder's MCP endpoint.
verdict: Avoid for new setups: the official README marks it deprecated; use it only on existing installs.

name: Netlify MCP Server
agentsSource: clients listed with install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Creates, deploys and manages sites in your Netlify account.
credentials: Netlify account login; a Personal Access Token only as a temporary auth workaround, as documented.
install: Add `npx -y @netlify/mcp` to your client's MCP config (see README).
verdict: Pick it to build and deploy Netlify sites from the agent; it authenticates with your Netlify account.

name: Heroku Platform MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with an example configuration in the official README
permissions: Manages Heroku apps, add-ons and resources with your Heroku CLI identity.
credentials: Heroku CLI login (`heroku mcp:start`) or HEROKU_API_KEY.
install: Run `heroku mcp:start` from your client's MCP config, or `npx -y @heroku/mcp-server` with HEROKU_API_KEY (see README).
verdict: Pick it to manage Heroku apps from the agent; the README recommends `heroku mcp:start` so you don't expose an API key.

name: Atlassian Rovo MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Reads and writes Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket Cloud, Compass, Loom and other Atlassian Cloud data within your existing Atlassian permissions; org admins enable or revoke permission groups (read/write/search).
credentials: Atlassian Cloud account via OAuth 2.1, or a scoped API token (an org admin must enable API-token auth; Jira Service Management tools are API-token only).
install: Cloud-hosted: point your client at `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp` (Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`); see README for other clients.
verdict: Pick it when the agent must read or update Jira issues, Confluence pages or Bitbucket repos; the README recommends the v2 endpoint for new setups.

name: Next.js DevTools MCP
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Discovers local Next.js 16+ dev servers and proxies their built-in `/_next/mcp` tools (errors, routes, logs, Server Actions); sends anonymous usage telemetry unless NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1.
credentials: None
install: Run `npx -y next-devtools-mcp@latest` from your client's MCP config, or `npx add-mcp next-devtools-mcp@latest` (see README).
license: MIT (stated in README; GitHub detects no LICENSE file)
verdict: Pick it to let the agent read live errors, routes and logs from a running Next.js 16+ dev server; it needs `npm run dev` running.

name: Redis MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Reads and writes Redis data (strings, hashes, lists, sets, streams, JSON, vector search) with the connection's ACL rights; the README shows how to use a read-only ACL user.
credentials: Redis connection URL or REDIS_HOST/REDIS_PORT plus REDIS_USERNAME/REDIS_PWD when auth is enabled; Entra ID for Azure Managed Redis.
install: Run `uvx --from redis-mcp-server@latest redis-mcp-server --url redis://localhost:6379/0` from your client's MCP config (see README).
verdict: Pick it to let the agent inspect or cache data in Redis; connect it with a read-only ACL user unless writes are intended.

name: SonarQube MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Reads issues, quality gates, measures, security hotspots, coverage and rules from SonarQube Cloud or Server with the token's rights, and can analyze file content; some tools write (e.g. changing issue status) unless SONARQUBE_READ_ONLY=true. Sends anonymous usage telemetry unless TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true.
credentials: SonarQube user token (SONARQUBE_TOKEN) plus SONARQUBE_ORG for SonarQube Cloud or SONARQUBE_URL for SonarQube Server.
install: Run the `sonarsource/sonarqube-mcp` container from your client's MCP config (e.g. `claude mcp add sonarqube`), or use the official configuration generator (see README).
license: SONAR Source-Available License v1.0 (per LICENSE; GitHub detects no SPDX license)
verdict: Pick it if your project already runs on SonarQube Cloud or Server and you want the agent to read issues and quality gates during review; set SONARQUBE_READ_ONLY=true for review-only use.

name: Microsoft Learn MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup heading or install/config instructions in the official README
permissions: Read-only tools: searches and fetches Microsoft Learn documentation and official code samples through Microsoft's hosted remote endpoint, so your queries go to that service.
credentials: None (README: no API key or sign-in required).
install: Add the remote endpoint https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp in your client (e.g. `codex mcp add "microsoft-learn" --url "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp"`), or use the one-click installs in the README.
license: MIT for code (LICENSE-CODE); CC-BY-4.0 for docs (LICENSE)
verdict: Pick it when the agent writes Azure, .NET or other Microsoft code and should look up current official docs and samples; it needs no credentials.

name: Buildkite MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup section in Buildkite's official remote MCP server docs (buildkite.com/docs/apis/mcp-server)
permissions: Reads pipelines, builds, jobs, logs, annotations and test results; with write scopes it can retry jobs or start builds, which can run pipeline commands. A read-only remote endpoint and the --read-only flag exclude mutating tools.
credentials: Buildkite OAuth on the hosted remote server, or a Buildkite API access token (BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN) for the local server.
install: Connect your client to Buildkite's hosted remote MCP server (OAuth), or run the local `buildkite-mcp-server stdio` with BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN (see the official docs).
verdict: Pick it to let the agent investigate failed Buildkite builds and logs; use the read-only endpoint unless you want it to retry jobs or start builds.

name: Datadog MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup tab in Datadog's official MCP setup docs (docs.datadoghq.com/mcp_server/setup); GitHub README shows Claude Code quick start
permissions: Queries Datadog observability data (logs, metrics, traces, monitors, dashboards, security signals and more) and can perform write actions that the authenticated user's Datadog permissions allow; write tools are rejected for read-only users.
credentials: Datadog OAuth (recommended) or Datadog API and application keys for some clients.
maintenance: Managed remote server; no GitHub release on datadog-labs/mcp-server; CHANGELOG updated through 2026-10-15; last commit 2026-10-16
install: Use `claude mcp add --transport http datadog` with the US1 URL https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp (or your regional endpoint), or install the Datadog plugin/connector for your client (see setup docs).
verdict: Pick it to investigate production issues from the agent using your Datadog account; OAuth keeps access within your existing RBAC.

name: Figma MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup section in Figma's official MCP server guide README
permissions: Reads Figma design context (frames, components, variables, layout) and can write to the canvas or generate/upload images when those tools are enabled; write-to-canvas is in a free beta that Figma says will become usage-based later.
credentials: Figma account OAuth when connecting the remote server (client-specific auth, e.g. `/mcp auth figma` in Gemini CLI).
maintenance: Hosted remote server (MCP Registry / server.json version 2.2.157); guide repo last commit 2026-10-19; no GitHub release
install: Connect to https://mcp.figma.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP). Examples: `claude mcp add --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`, or install via `gemini extensions install` from https://github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide (see README).
license: Not stated (guide repository has no LICENSE file)
verdict: Pick it to pull design context into code or (in beta) write back to the Figma canvas; you need a Figma account and a client that supports remote Streamable HTTP.

name: MCP Toolbox for Databases
agentsSource: clients named with MCP configuration instructions in the official README (Gemini CLI has dedicated install steps; others are listed for the prebuilt MCP server)
permissions: Runs database tools you configure (prebuilt generic tools such as list_tables/execute_sql, or custom toolsets): can read schemas and run SQL against the connected sources with the credentials you give the Toolbox process.
credentials: Database connection env vars for the chosen prebuilt source (see Prebuilt Tools Reference); Google Cloud sources can use Application Default Credentials / IAM.
install: Run `npx -y @toolbox-sdk/server --prebuilt=postgres --stdio` (other `--prebuilt` databases in the README), or install the binary and point your MCP client at the local Toolbox HTTP endpoint shown in the README Connect section.
verdict: Pick it to explore schemas and run SQL from the agent across many databases (Postgres, BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Spanner and others); prefer custom toolsets when you need restricted queries in production.
